tool.name: agent_finish
tool.description:
Mark a subagent's task as completed and optionally report results to parent agent.
IMPORTANT: This tool can ONLY be used by subagents (agents with a parent). Root/main agents must use finish_scan instead.
This tool should be called when a subagent completes its assigned subtask to: - Mark the subagent's task as completed - Report findings back to the parent agent
Use this tool when: - You are a subagent working on a specific subtask - You have completed your assigned task - You want to report your findings to the parent agent - You are ready to terminate this subagent's execution
tool.details: This replaces the previous finish_scan tool and handles both sub-agent completion and main agent completion. When a sub-agent finishes, it can report its findings back to the parent agent for coordination.

parameter.name: result_summary
parameter.description: Summary of what the agent accomplished and discovered

parameter.name: findings
parameter.description: List of specific findings, vulnerabilities, or discoveries

parameter.name: success
parameter.description: Whether the agent's task completed successfully

parameter.name: report_to_parent
parameter.description: Whether to send results back to the parent agent

parameter.name: final_recommendations
parameter.description: Recommendations for next steps or follow-up actions

returns.description: Response containing: - agent_completed: Whether the agent was marked as completed - parent_notified: Whether parent was notified (if applicable) - completion_summary: Summary of completion status

tool.examples:
# Sub-agent completing subdomain enumeration task
Completed comprehensive subdomain enumeration for target.com. Discovered 47 subdomains including several interesting ones with admin/dev in the name. Found 3 subdomains with exposed services on non-standard ports. ["admin.target.com - exposed phpMyAdmin", "dev-api.target.com - unauth API endpoints", "staging.target.com - directory listing enabled", "mail.target.com - POP3/IMAP services"] true true ["Prioritize testing admin.target.com for default creds", "Enumerate dev-api.target.com API endpoints", "Check staging.target.com for sensitive files"]

tool.name: create_agent
tool.description:
Create and spawn a new agent to handle a specific subtask.
Only create a new agent if no existing agent is handling the specific task.
tool.details:
The new agent starts with a FRESH context by default. You (the parent) are responsible for packing everything the child needs into the `task` and an optional structured `briefing` — prior findings, target scope, file paths to read, etc. The child can also read files from the shared /workspace directory and see proxy traffic from previous work.
Select a `role` to scope the child's system prompt to its phase (e.g. recon vs exploit vs report). A focused role means a shorter, more relevant system prompt and better specialization.
Valid roles: pre-recon, recon, vuln-injection, vuln-xss, vuln-auth, vuln-authz, vuln-ssrf, exploit-injection, exploit-xss, exploit-auth, exploit-authz, exploit-ssrf, report. Omit `role` for a generalist child that inherits the full orchestrator prompt.
The agent runs asynchronously and independently, allowing the parent to continue immediately while the new agent executes its task in the background.
If you as a parent agent don't absolutely have anything to do while your subagents are running, you can use wait_for_message tool. The subagent will continue to run in the background, and update you when it's done.

parameter.name: task
parameter.description: The specific task/objective for the new agent to accomplish. Must be self-contained — the child does NOT see your conversation history by default.

parameter.name: name
parameter.description: Human-readable name for the agent (for tracking purposes)

parameter.name: role
parameter.description: Phase-scoped role for the child. Selects a focused system prompt. Valid values: pre-recon, recon, vuln-injection, vuln-xss, vuln-auth, vuln-authz, vuln-ssrf, exploit-injection, exploit-xss, exploit-auth, exploit-authz, exploit-ssrf, report. When role is vuln-* or exploit-*, the matching skill is auto-added to `skills`. Omit for a generalist agent.

parameter.name: briefing
parameter.description: Structured briefing of what the child needs to know — prior findings, target scope, file paths to read, confirmed inputs/outputs. Prefer this over inherit_context; it's cheaper and clearer. Markdown or JSON both fine.

parameter.name: inherit_context
parameter.description: Escape hatch: if true, injects the parent's full conversation history into the child. Default is FALSE. Almost always leave this unset and pass a concise `briefing` instead — full history inheritance is expensive and usually unnecessary.

parameter.name: skills
parameter.description: Comma-separated list of skills to use for the agent (MAXIMUM 5 skills allowed). Most agents should have at least one skill in order to be useful. Agents should be highly specialized - use 1-3 related skills; up to 5 for complex contexts. {{DYNAMIC_SKILLS_DESCRIPTION}}

returns.description: Response containing: - agent_id: Unique identifier for the created agent - success: Whether the agent was created successfully - message: Status message - agent_info: Details about the created agent

tool.examples:
# Spawn a recon agent with a concise briefing (no full-history inheritance)
Map the attack surface for the deployed web app: enumerate subdomains, open ports, tech stack, all reachable endpoints and their parameters. Write the map via write_deliverable at path="recon/attack_surface.md". Recon Agent recon Target: https://example.com (authorized for full pentest). Scope: *.example.com subdomains + main app only; no third-party SaaS. Prior work: none yet — you are the first agent in the pipeline.
# Spawn a vuln-discovery specialist with a type-scoped role
Identify XSS sinks in the /search and /comments endpoints. For each suspected sink, trace source → sink and write a finding via write_deliverable at path="findings/xss/<id>.md" (one deliverable per finding). XSS Discovery Agent vuln-xss Target map deliverable: recon/attack_surface.md (use read_deliverable). Focus endpoints: GET /search?q=, POST /comments. Both echo user input in HTML body. Auth required for /comments — test credentials stored in /workspace/creds.env.
# Spawn an exploit-phase validator for a specific finding
Build a working PoC for the reflected XSS in /search?q=. Capture the payload, the HTTP request, and evidence of execution (cookie exfil or JS alert). Save via write_deliverable at path="pocs/xss-search.md". XSS Exploit Validator exploit-xss Finding deliverable to validate: findings/xss/001.md (read_deliverable). Summary: <script> reflected unsanitized in search result page, context = HTML body, no CSP. Try basic alert() payload first, then cookie exfil variant.
# Spawn a reporting agent — needs only the confirmed finding + PoC
Write a formal vulnerability report for the confirmed reflected XSS using create_vulnerability_report. Include severity, CWE, reproduction steps, impact. XSS Reporter report Confirmed finding deliverable: findings/xss/001.md. PoC deliverable: pocs/xss-search.md. Read both with read_deliverable. Severity rationale: session cookie not HttpOnly; cookie exfil PoC succeeded.

tool.name: send_message_to_agent
tool.description: Send a message to another agent in the graph for coordination and communication.
tool.details:
This enables agents to communicate with each other during execution, but should be used only when essential: - Sharing discovered information or findings - Asking questions or requesting assistance - Providing instructions or coordination - Reporting status or results
Best practices: - Avoid routine status updates; batch non-urgent information - Prefer parent/child completion flows (agent_finish) - Do not message when the context is already known

parameter.name: target_agent_id
parameter.description: ID of the agent to send the message to

parameter.name: message_type
parameter.description: Type of message being sent: - "query": Question requiring a response - "instruction": Command or directive for the target agent - "information": Informational message (findings, status, etc.)

returns.description: Response containing: - success: Whether the message was sent successfully - message_id: Unique identifier for the message - delivery_status: Status of message delivery

tool.examples:
# Share discovered vulnerability information
agent_abc123 Found SQL injection vulnerability in /login.php parameter 'username'. Payload: admin' OR '1'='1' -- successfully bypassed authentication. You should focus your testing on the authenticated areas of the application. information high
# Request assistance from specialist agent
agent_def456 I've identified what appears to be a custom encryption implementation in the API responses. Can you analyze the cryptographic strength and look for potential weaknesses? query normal

tool.name: view_agent_graph
tool.description: View the current agent graph showing all agents, their relationships, and status.
tool.details: This provides a comprehensive overview of the multi-agent system including: - All agent nodes with their tasks, status, and metadata - Parent-child relationships between agents - Message communication patterns - Current execution state

returns.description: Response containing: - graph_structure: Human-readable representation of the agent graph - summary: High-level statistics about the graph

tool.name: wait_for_message
tool.description:
Pause the agent loop indefinitely until receiving a message from another agent.
This tool puts the agent into a waiting state where it remains idle until it receives any form of communication. The agent will automatically resume execution when a message arrives.
IMPORTANT: This tool causes the agent to stop all activity until a message is received. Use it when you need to: - Wait for subagent completion reports - Coordinate with other agents before proceeding - Synchronize multi-agent workflows
NOTE: If you are waiting for an agent that is NOT your subagent, you first tell it to message you with updates before waiting for it. Otherwise, you will wait forever!
tool.details:
When this tool is called, the agent (you) enters a waiting state and will not continue execution until: - Another agent sends a message via send_message_to_agent - Any other form of inter-agent communication occurs - Waiting timeout is reached
The agent will automatically resume from where it left off once a message is received. This is particularly useful for parent agents waiting for subagent results or for coordination points in multi-agent workflows. NOTE: If you finished your task, and you do NOT have any child agents running, you should NEVER use this tool, and just call finish tool instead.

parameter.name: reason
parameter.description: Explanation for why the agent is waiting (for logging and monitoring purposes)

returns.description: Response containing: - success: Whether the agent successfully entered waiting state - status: Current agent status ("waiting") - reason: The reason for waiting - agent_info: Details about the waiting agent - resume_conditions: List of conditions that will resume the agent

tool.examples:
# Wait for subagents to complete their tasks
Waiting for subdomain enumeration and port scanning subagents to complete their tasks and report findings
# Coordinate with other agents
Waiting for vulnerability assessment agent to share discovered attack vectors before proceeding with exploitation phase
